title: Large integral rho tensor squares detect primitive fixed vectors
statement: Let $A$ be a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring] with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ and algebraically closed residue field $\kappa=A/\mathfrak m$. Let $H$ be a smooth affine finitely presented group scheme over $\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, pqf-def-affine-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-weil-affine-spectrum], with the group-object diagrams over this base. Suppose $H$ is split semisimple simply connected: its geometric fibres are connected and have no nontrivial smooth connected solvable normal subgroup, every central isogeny onto such a fibre from a connected semisimple group is an isomorphism, and choose a split maximal torus $T\subseteq H$ and a Borel subgroup scheme $B\supseteq T$. Here a central isogeny is a surjective group homomorphism with finite central kernel; solvable means that the iterated derived subgroups eventually become trivial; a split torus is a group scheme isomorphic to a product of copies of $\mathbf G_m$; maximal tori and Borel subgroup schemes have, on each geometric fibre, a maximal torus and a maximal smooth connected solvable subgroup, respectively. Write $\mathbf G_m(C)=C^\times$ for every commutative $A$-algebra $C$. A character is a homomorphism of group schemes to $\mathbf G_m$. Let $\Phi^+$ be the positive roots determined by $B$, namely the nonzero characters occurring in the adjoint $T$-action on $\operatorname{Lie}(B)$; the latter is the tangent module at the identity, defined by dual-number points reducing to the identity. In the character lattice $X^*(T)$, addition means multiplication of character values. Use the rational section modules of [lem-sfb-dvr-rho-section-modules], with the following explicit description. Let $\rho\in X^*(T)$ satisfy $2\rho=\sum_{\alpha\in\Phi^+}\alpha$, and let $\widetilde\rho:B\to\mathbf G_m$ extend $\rho$ and be trivial on the unipotent radical of $B$. This radical is the subgroup whose geometric fibres are the largest smooth connected normal unipotent subgroups; unipotent means that all geometric points become unipotent matrices in a faithful linear representation. For every integer $m\ge1$, put $$W_m=\{f\in A[H]:f(gb)=\widetilde\rho(b)^m f(g)\text{ for all commutative }A\text{-algebras }C,\ g\in H(C),\ b\in B(C)\}.$$ Evaluation of $f$ means pullback of the regular function along its $C$-point. Use the left-translation action $(h f)(g)=f(h^{-1}g)$. A rational $H$-module is an $A$-module $M$ with an $A$-linear coaction $M\to M\otimes_A A[H]$ satisfying the counit and coassociativity identities, where $A[H]=\Gamma(H,\mathcal O_H)$ is the coordinate Hopf algebra. Its invariants are $M^H=\{x:\rho_M(x)=x\otimes1\}$. Equivariant maps commute with coactions; tensor products have diagonal coaction. These identities are tested after every commutative $A$-algebra extension, not just on $A$-points. For every finite free rational $H$-module $V$ and every $v\in V^H$ such that $v\notin\mathfrak mV$, there exists an integer $M\ge1$ such that for every $m\ge M$ there is an equivariant $A$-linear map $$a_m:V\longrightarrow W_m\otimes_A W_m$$ whose value at $v$ has nonzero image in $(W_m\otimes_A W_m)\otimes_A\kappa$. The bound $M$ may depend on $V$ and $v$.

source.place: Lemma 9.7.2(2), printed pp.526--527; Seshadri Property I(b), p.247. The necessary condition v not in the maximal ideal times V is explicit here: v=0 or v in mV cannot have nonzero reduction under any A-linear map. Local PDF WANTED; primary published PDF and arXiv HTML read online.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-dvr-double-flag-invariant-boundary] to the given $A,H,T,B,\rho,\widetilde\rho$. Obtain $Q,L,X,D,d,U,q$ with the stated diagonal actions, integral quasi-compact separated $X$, dense stable $U$, nonempty $U_\kappa$, and $\Gamma(Q,L^m)=W_m$. We use its equivariant identification $\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)=A[H]^{T,\mathrm{right}}$.

source.place: Lemma 9.7.2(2), printed pp.526--527. Agent-written integral double-flag proof; the source states Property I(b) without its proof. Local Alper and Seshadri copies WANTED; published Alper PDF read online.

proof.text: Choose a finite basis $(e_i)$ of $V$. Since $v\notin\mathfrak mV$, one coordinate $v_j$ is outside the maximal ideal, hence a unit in the local ring $A$. The functional $\ell(u)=v_j^{-1}u_j$ has $\ell(v)=1$. Apply [lem-sfb-relative-torus-bundle-weights] to the restricted coaction of the split torus $T\simeq\mathbf G_m^r$ on the finite free (hence finite projective) module $V$. Its direct-sum decomposition gives the projection $p_0$ to weight zero. Since $v$ is fixed by $H$, it has weight zero. Thus $\lambda=\ell p_0$ satisfies $\lambda(v)=1$ and is $T$-invariant as a coaction identity. No freeness of the weight-zero summand is needed.

source.place: Lemma 9.7.2(2), printed pp.526--527. Agent-written integral double-flag proof; the source states Property I(b) without its proof. Local Alper and Seshadri copies WANTED; published Alper PDF read online.

proof.text: For $u\in V$ set $c(u)(g)=\lambda(g^{-1}u)$. The coaction, group inversion and the linear functional make this a regular function. For every commutative $A$-algebra $C$, $c(u)(gt)=\lambda(t^{-1}g^{-1}u)=c(u)(g)$ and $c(hu)(g)=c(u)(h^{-1}g)$. Consequently the identification in Step 1 gives an equivariant map $c:V\to\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$, and $c(v)=1$. The equations hold at universal points, so they are coaction equations.

source.place: Lemma 9.7.2(2), printed pp.526--527. Agent-written integral double-flag proof; the source states Property I(b) without its proof. Local Alper and Seshadri copies WANTED; published Alper PDF read online.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-invert-s-cohomology] with its scheme $X$, invertible sheaf $D$, section $d$, quasi-coherent sheaf $\mathcal O_X$ and $p=0$. Step 1 supplies quasi-compactness and separatedness (hence quasi-separatedness). For each basis element $e_i$, write $c(e_i)=b_i/d^{n_i}$ with $n_i\ge0$ and $b_i\in\Gamma(X,D^{n_i})$. Set $N=\max(1,n_1,\ldots,n_{\operatorname{rank}V})$. For each integer $m\ge N$, define an $A$-linear map $b_m:V\to\Gamma(X,D^m)$ by $b_m(e_i)=d^{m-n_i}b_i$. Its restriction to $U$ is $d^mc$. Thus a single finite maximum works for every integer $m\ge N$.

source.place: Tag 09MR, lemma-invert-s-cohomology, degree p=0; finite common denominator argument.

proof.text: Restriction $r_m:\Gamma(X,D^m)\to\Gamma(U,D^m)$ is injective: in an affine trivialization of $D^m$ on the integral scheme $X$, its coefficient is in a domain, and vanishing on a dense open forces that coefficient to be zero. By [sbc-lem-smooth-criterion], $H\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is flat; [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-affine-criterion] on these affine schemes makes $A[H]$ a flat $A$-module. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] makes $r_m\otimes_A1_{A[H]}$ injective. On $U$, the equation $b_m=d^mc$, invariance of $d$, equivariance of $c$, and multiplicativity of the induced coactions for the $\mathcal O_U$-module structure of $\Gamma(U,D^m)$ (coactions are pullback along the action morphism) show that the two sides of the coaction equation for $b_m$ agree. Restriction commutes with coactions by Step 1, and this tensor injection proves the equation on $X$. Hence $b_m$ is equivariant. The same injectivity applied to $b_m(v)|_U=d^m|_U$ gives $b_m(v)=d^m$.

source.place: Lemma 9.7.2(2), printed pp.526--527. Agent-written integral double-flag proof; the source states Property I(b) without its proof. Local Alper and Seshadri copies WANTED; published Alper PDF read online.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-dvr-external-invertible-global-sections] to $Q,Q,L^m,L^m$. By Step 1, $Q$ is smooth and projective over $A$ with linearized $L$. Smoothness gives flatness of $Q\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ by [sbc-lem-smooth-criterion]; projectivity (a closed immersion into $\mathbf P^n_A$, with quasi-compact structure map) gives quasi-compactness and separatedness. Tensor powers of an invertible sheaf are invertible by multiplying rank-one local trivializations. The resulting external-section isomorphism, together with $\Gamma(Q,L^m)=W_m$, gives an equivariant $A$-linear isomorphism $K_m:W_m\otimes_AW_m\simeq\Gamma(X,D^m)$. Put $a_m=K_m^{-1}b_m$.

source.place: Lemma 9.7.2(2), printed pp.526--527. Agent-written integral double-flag proof; the source states Property I(b) without its proof. Local Alper and Seshadri copies WANTED; published Alper PDF read online.

proof.text: If $a_m(v)$ had zero image modulo $\mathfrak m$, every coefficient in a finite basis of $W_m\otimes_AW_m$ would lie in $\mathfrak m=(\pi)$, so $a_m(v)=\pi z$. Such a basis exists by [lem-sfb-dvr-rho-section-modules], taking pairwise tensors of bases. Then $d^m=b_m(v)=\pi K_m(z)$, whose pullback to the special fibre $X_\kappa$ would vanish. But $d^m$ is nowhere vanishing on the nonempty open $U_\kappa$ by Step 1, a contradiction. Thus the value of $a_m$ has nonzero residual image for every $m\ge N$; take $M=N$.
